I'm Triaging My Inbox with Joule Desktop

How we built a custom skill to classify emails, surface what's urgent, and generate draft replies — without engineering support, infrastructure, or write permissions on the mailbox.

By Chris O'Hara · 10 min read

Most of us start the day the same way: staring at an inbox that filled up overnight, trying to figure out what actually needs attention before the first meeting. The volume isn't the problem — it's the cognitive load of classifying, prioritizing, and deciding what to do with each message. By the time you've triaged manually, half your morning is gone.

We wanted an AI agent that could handle that triage automatically — classify what's urgent, flag what needs a response, and generate ready-to-paste drafts for everything that does. The question was how to get there without a multi-month implementation project.

The Easy Way and the Hard Way

There are two paths to inbox automation, and both are worth it — which one you choose depends on volume, urgency, and how much infrastructure you're willing to maintain.

The hard way is full automation: a custom agent or Microsoft Power Automate workflow that runs on a schedule, writes drafts directly to Outlook, and requires no daily prompting. It's the right answer for high-volume executive mailboxes where even "triage my inbox" is too much friction. But it requires Graph API write permissions, security review, and ongoing maintenance.

The easy way is a Joule Desktop Skill — a plain Markdown file that tells Joule how to triage your email when you ask. No infrastructure, no write permissions, no engineers. You prompt it each morning ("triage my inbox"), and it returns a classified digest with draft replies you can copy-paste. You give up automation; you gain speed to value.

We started with the easy way — and got to 80% of the value in an afternoon. For most people, that's enough. For high-volume mailboxes, the hard way is worth the investment. But here's the thing: building Joule skills is one of the fastest paths to successful AI adoption. You learn the patterns, see immediate results, and build confidence before tackling the bigger automation projects.

This is how we built the inbox triage skill.

Comparing the Approaches

Here's how the options stack up:

Option Pro Con
Custom inbox-agent (Python) Full automation, writes back to Outlook Requires hosting, maintenance, Graph API write perms
Microsoft Power Automate + AI Builder Native, production-grade, fully automatic More setup time, requires IT involvement for licensing
Joule Desktop + Skill Fast to deploy, no infrastructure, no write perms needed Read-only; must prompt manually each morning

The trade-off is simple: type "triage my inbox" each morning instead of having it run automatically. In exchange, you deploy in hours instead of weeks, with no security review and no IT ticket. The Power Automate path remains the right upgrade when full automation becomes necessary — but for getting started, the Joule Desktop approach gets you to value immediately.

Step 1: Register the App in Microsoft Entra ID

Joule Desktop's email integration runs through Microsoft Graph. To connect it to the right mailbox context, we registered an Azure application via SAP's internal provisioning process.

How to request an Entra app registration at SAP:

  1. Go to itsupport.sap.com
  2. Open a ticket under category: Azure: Entra App Registration
  3. Provide: app name, business justification, and the owner(s) to assign

We created two apps during the pilot process:

App Name Client ID Purpose
CMO-Inbox-Automation-Pilot 875d7149-579f-4f4c-bc55-d8ae995331dd Initial pilot registration
inbox-automation e76d6f06-c513-4dfa-8d80-2f3eb6d88cb2 Final registered app

The SAP Global Authentication Team provisions these automatically. Confirmation arrives via email from auth@global.corp.sap with the Client ID, Object ID, and Service Principal ID.

Note: IT may request additional information before completing the registration. Ticket INC32925982 required a follow-up response before the solution was proposed. Check itsupport.sap.com for status.

To manage the app after creation:

  1. Request the Azure Portal access package (auto-approved): myaccess.microsoft.com/@sap.onmicrosoft.com
  2. Once approved, go to: Azure Portal → Azure Active Directory → App Registrations
  3. Search for your app name and configure permissions as needed

Step 2: Install Joule Desktop

  1. Download Joule Work Desktop from the SAP internal software portal
  2. Sign in with your SAP corporate credentials (SSO via Microsoft Entra ID)
  3. Joule automatically connects to your Microsoft 365 mailbox and calendar via the built-in Graph integration — no additional configuration needed for read access

Key constraint: Joule Desktop's email access is read-only by design. It can read, search, and summarize emails, but cannot send, label, or create drafts in Outlook. This is intentional — it keeps the integration simple and avoids requiring broad Graph API write permissions.

Step 3: Write the Skill

Skills in Joule Desktop are plain Markdown files that tell Joule how to handle a specific type of request. The inbox triage skill lives at:

[Joule Desktop app directory]/skills/inbox-triage/SKILL.md

The skill has two parts:

Part A: Frontmatter (YAML header)

Defines the skill name, description, and the trigger phrases Joule listens for:

---
name: inbox-triage
description: >-
  Triages unread email from the past 12 hours. Classifies messages into
  Urgent, Needs-reply, FYI, Newsletter, and Sensitive buckets, then
  generates ready-to-paste reply drafts for all items that need a response.
  Use when the user says: "triage my inbox", "what needs my attention",
  "morning briefing", "email digest", "catch me up on email", etc.
---

Part B: Instructions (Markdown body)

Step-by-step instructions Joule follows when the skill activates:

  1. Fetch — Call list_emails with onlyUnread: true, top: 50. Filter to the last 12 hours.
  2. Read — For emails that look urgent or need a reply, call get_email in parallel to read the full body. Skip automated/bulk mail.
  3. Classify — Sort each email into one of five buckets:
    • 🔴 Urgent — needs a decision or response today
    • 📬 Needs Reply — requires a response, not necessarily today
    • 📋 FYI — informational, no reply needed
    • 📰 Newsletter / Bulk — automated or marketing mail
    • ⚠️ Sensitive — flagged keywords; never drafted, surfaced for manual review only
  4. Output — Produce a structured digest with summaries, recommended actions, and ready-to-paste draft replies for all Needs Reply items.

Sensitive keyword list (built into the skill):

board, legal, confidential, personnel, hr, human resources, offer letter, acquisition, merger, press, media inquiry, layoff, termination, compensation, salary, bonus, lawsuit, nda, non-disclosure

Step 4: Test the Skill

  1. Open Joule Desktop
  2. Type: "triage my inbox"
  3. Joule activates the skill, fetches unread emails, classifies them, and returns the digest

If there are no unread emails in the 12-hour window, Joule responds: "No unread emails in the last 12 hours. Inbox is clear."

You can also ask for a broader summary — covering all recent emails regardless of read status — by prompting: "give me the summary anyway."

What Success Looks Like

Here's an actual morning triage session. The skill processed 12 unread emails and generated draft replies for each one that needed a response:

Draft replies generated by the inbox triage skill, ready to review and send

Each draft includes the recipient, subject line, a contextually appropriate response, and — critically — a note flagging anything that needs human review before sending. The Cara Turbyfill email, for example, was flagged as sensitive (HR/confidential) and marked for manual review rather than auto-drafted.

The drafts aren't perfect, but they don't need to be. They give you a starting point that's 80% there — which turns a 45-minute morning triage into a 10-minute review and send session.

What the Skill Does NOT Do

This is important to set expectations with end users:

Capability Joule Desktop Skill
Read and summarize emails ✅
Generate draft reply text in chat ✅
Flag sensitive items ✅
Apply labels or categories in Outlook ❌ Read-only
Create drafts in Outlook Drafts folder ❌ Read-only
Send emails automatically ❌ Read-only
Run on a schedule without prompting ❌ Must be triggered manually

What's Next: The Path to Full Automation

If the end user needs the triage to run automatically and write back to Outlook, the recommended path is Microsoft Power Automate + AI Builder. This is the Microsoft-native production approach. It requires:

  • Power Automate license (included in most M365 E3/E5 plans)
  • AI Builder credits for the classification step
  • Mailbox delegation or shared mailbox access for the EA

The Joule Desktop skill is a fast, zero-infrastructure way to get started. The Power Automate path is the right upgrade when scheduling and write-back become requirements.
